title: The Empty Point Practice
opening: Notice what is here without beginning with an order to change it. You can begin, pause or stop when you choose.

labels.application: When you are ready to respond

steps: Sit quietly and begin with simple statements such as “I notice traffic” or “I notice a thought about dinner.”
Acknowledge sensations, thoughts, emotions and the urge to fix them.
Notice the noticing itself: “I notice I am aware of these sensations.”
Let the statements slow if they slow naturally; do not force an empty mind.
Notice an insight or impulse to act and examine the situation it concerns.
notePrompt: If you want to save something for yourself, note what you noticed or what situation may need a response. You can stop or act without writing a note.
application: Relief may happen, but it is not a required result. You may notice a boundary to establish, a conversation to have or a difficulty you do not want to keep accepting. Permanent neutrality is not required. If the next action is already clear, take it without a sitting practice first.
sourceExcerpt: This practice may bring relief. It may also show you a boundary to establish, a conversation to have or a difficulty you do not want to keep accepting. Emotional mastery includes responding to those findings. It does not require permanent neutrality.
